analysis.title: Nordic Outlook Update – USA (November 2026)
key_insights: SEB raises its US GDP forecast again, to 2.4% in 2026, 2.3% in 2027 and 2.2% in 2028. That is 0.2 percentage points above the August Nordic Outlook for 2026 and 2027, and 0.1 above for 2028.
Business sentiment (ISM and PMI) improved further after the start of the war with Iran and points to continued solid growth. SEB does not expect the Q3 boom to continue.
Q3 GDP grew by nearly 3.5% q/q annualized. Private domestic demand (household consumption and business investment) rose by nearly 5%. SEB expects growth to slow to a trend-like 2% q/q pace in 2027.

Fiscal support limited the hit to consumption from higher gasoline prices, but the effect is fading. Sluggish employment growth, falling real earnings and weak consumer sentiment point to a slowdown in coming quarters.

Household spending has outpaced real disposable income because unusually large tax refunds offset high gasoline prices in the first half of 2026. The savings ratio has fallen below its historical average.
Wealth effects from rising equity prices support spending but make consumption sensitive to setbacks in AI.

Data center investment is expected to keep rising quickly, although higher borrowing costs could weigh on some plans. The AI effect on total GDP is reduced by a large import share. More generous tax depreciation rules may have contributed to broader investment. Residential construction keeps declining because of high mortgage rates.

The labour market is in a low-hiring, no-firing state. Unemployment is stable slightly above 4%, around the Fed's view of the longer run. Job creation has picked up from the 2025 lows but is well below the pre-pandemic average. Tight immigration policy and an aging population limit labour supply growth.
AI has had visible negative employment effects in information and finance, partly offset by job gains in other sectors such as manufacturing.

SEB treats the upward pressure on inflation from tariffs, energy prices and AI-related IT prices as temporary. A prolonged period of elevated energy prices risks spreading into other prices. Core inflation forecast for 2027 is raised slightly. Inflation has been above target for over 5 years.
Wage growth of about 3-3.5% and strong productivity growth support a return to the 2% inflation target by end 2028.
SEB expects one more Fed rate hike in December 2026, then a cut in late 2027 and two more cuts in the first half of 2028. Markets price two additional hikes through end 2027.

Democrats won both chambers in the midterms. SEB expects gridlock and slightly more expansionary fiscal policy, but no room for major new spending or tax cuts. Democratic governors in some states may temporarily slow the AI build-out. SEB says Fed independence will come under less pressure after the Senate shift.

sector_views.rationale: Data center investment is expected to keep rising rapidly, though higher borrowing costs could weigh on some plans and a large import share limits the GDP effect.
Activity continues to decline because of high mortgage rates.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price two additional hikes through end 2027, which reflects expectations of sticky inflation and resilient growth.
tension_points.bear_case: SEB expects only one more hike in December 2026, then a cut in late 2027 and two cuts in H1 2028. It sees underlying inflation contained by slowing job creation and modest wage growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A prolonged period of elevated energy prices spreading into other prices would favour the market's more hawkish path.
